events.title: Neolithic Settlement
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human settlement in Bahrain during Neolithic period. Early inhabitants utilized Bahrain's freshwater springs (rare in Persian Gulf) and abundant marine resources.

events.title: Dilmun Civilization Flourishing
events.description: Bahrain was center of ancient Dilmun civilization, important trade hub between Mesopotamia, Indus Valley and Arabia. Dilmun described in Sumerian epics as 'sacred land' and 'land of immortality.' Bahrain's seals and archaeological sites prove its prosperity and trade connections. Dilmun controlled copper trade and pearl industry, accumulating great wealth.

events.title: Dilmun Decline
events.description: Dilmun civilization declined, possibly due to trade route shifts and climate change. Bahrain was controlled by Kassites and later Assyrians, becoming peripheral province of regional empires.

events.title: Persian Achaemenid Rule
events.description: Bahrain was conquered by Persian Achaemenid Empire, becoming part of the empire. During Persian period Bahrain continued prospering as pearl and trade center.

events.title: Hellenistic Period
events.description: After Alexander the Great conquered Persia, Bahrain entered Hellenistic period. Greeks called Bahrain 'Tylos.' Greek merchants and settlers came to Bahrain, bringing Greek cultural influence. Archaeological discoveries include Greek-style architecture and coins.

events.title: Parthian Influence
events.description: Bahrain was influenced by Parthian Empire. Bahrain continued as important node in Persian Gulf trade, pearl industry continued prospering.

events.title: Sasanian Persian Rule
events.description: Bahrain was ruled by Persian Sasanian dynasty. During Sasanian period Bahrain was important pearl source. Nestorian Christianity spread in Bahrain, establishing churches and monasteries. Bahrain played role in Sasanian-Byzantine trade.

events.title: Islamic Conquest
events.description: Bahrain peacefully accepted Islam, one of first regions to convert. Bahrain played role in early Islam, participating in conquests and trade. Bahrain developed as important pearl trade center.

events.title: Qarmatian Rule
events.description: Shia Qarmatians established independent state based in Bahrain, controlling Eastern Arabia and Gulf trade. Qarmatians known for radical social egalitarianism, even attacked Mecca and stole Black Stone. They ruled for about two centuries.

events.title: Qarmatian Decline
events.description: Qarmatian state declined, Bahrain controlled by Seljuk Turks and Arab tribes. This began period of political instability and competition among multiple powers in Bahrain.

events.title: Usfurid Rule
events.description: Shia Usfurid dynasty controlled Bahrain and most of Eastern Arabia. They promoted pearl trade and agriculture, but also faced threats from Mongols and other powers.

events.title: Jabrids and Hormuz
events.description: Jabrid dynasty controlled Bahrain, later conquered by Persian Kingdom of Hormuz. Bahrain prospered under Hormuz rule, pearl trade reached peak.

events.title: Portuguese Arrival
events.description: Portuguese navy arrived in Persian Gulf, seeking to control trade routes. Portuguese first occupied Hormuz, then turned attention to Bahrain.

events.title: Portuguese Conquest
events.description: Portuguese conquered Bahrain, built fortresses to control Gulf trade. Portuguese rule lasted about 80 years, promoting trade links with Europe, but also causing local resistance.

events.title: Safavid Persia Conquest
events.description: Persian Safavid dynasty with British assistance expelled Portuguese and occupied Bahrain. Bahrain became territory under Persian Shia influence. Many Bahraini Shia Muslims trace their roots to Persian immigrants from this period.

events.title: Al Khalifa Conquest
events.description: Arab Sunni Al Khalifa family crossed from Qatar conquering Bahrain, seizing control from Persia. Al Khalifa established Bahrain emirate, ruling for over 240 years to today. This established pattern of Sunni royal family ruling Shia majority population, becoming source of Bahrain's political tensions.

events.title: Wahhabi and Omani Threats
events.description: Bahrain faced threats from Saudi Wahhabi movement and Oman. Al Khalifa family maneuvered among various powers, seeking British protection.

events.title: Treaty with Britain
events.description: Bahrain signed General Maritime Treaty with Britain, ending 'piracy' raids. Subsequent treaties made Bahrain British protectorate, Britain controlled foreign affairs and defense in exchange for protection.

events.title: Suez Canal Impact
events.description: After Suez Canal opening, Britain placed more importance on Persian Gulf. Bahrain's strategic position elevated as important British base in Gulf and pearl center.

events.title: Formal British Protectorate
events.description: Bahrain signed Perpetual Treaty of Peace and Friendship with Britain, formally establishing protectorate status. Britain protected Bahrain from Ottoman, Persian and Saudi threats. British advisors played important role in Bahrain government.

events.title: Pearl Industry Boom
events.description: Bahrain was most important pearl center in Persian Gulf, pearl industry was main economic pillar. Thousands engaged in pearl diving, Bahraini pearls renowned for quality. Manama developed as busy trading port.

events.title: Pearl Industry Collapse
events.description: Japanese cultured pearls destroyed Bahrain pearl industry, combined with Great Depression, Bahrain economy fell into crisis. Unemployment and poverty intensified, Bahrain urgently needed new economic source.

events.title: Oil Discovery
events.description: Oil discovered in Bahrain, first in Arabian Peninsula. Exports began 1934. Though reserves relatively small, oil transformed Bahrain economy, compensating for pearl industry collapse and enabling modernization.

events.title: Bahrain Petroleum Company (BAPCO)
events.description: Bahrain Petroleum Company established to develop oil resources. Oil revenues began flowing, government invested in infrastructure. Manama developed as modern city.

events.title: WWII and British Military Base
events.description: During WWII Bahrain was important British military base. After war Bahrain continued as Britain's main base in Gulf until 1971 independence.

events.title: Modernization and Social Change
events.description: Oil revenues enabled Bahrain modernization. Built schools, hospitals, roads. Education expanded, literacy rates increased. Foreign workers flooded in, especially from India and Pakistan. Bahrain developed as Gulf commercial and financial center.

events.title: Nationalism and Labor Movement
events.description: Nationalism and labor movements emerged in Bahrain, demanding political reform and better treatment. 1956 Bahrain workers struck demanding improved conditions. Government suppressed, but these movements laid foundation for later political activities.

events.title: British Withdrawal Announcement
events.description: Britain announced 1971 withdrawal from east of Suez. Bahrain faced independence and security challenges, especially Iran's sovereignty claims over Bahrain.

events.title: Federation Negotiations
events.description: After British withdrawal announcement, Bahrain negotiated with Qatar and Trucial Coast emirates to form federation. But due to disagreements, negotiations broke down. UN referendum confirmed Bahrainis wanted independence rather than belonging to Iran (Iran claimed sovereignty over Bahrain).

events.title: Iran Abandons Sovereignty Claim
events.description: UN investigation confirmed Bahrainis wanted independence. Iranian Shah under international pressure abandoned historical sovereignty claim over Bahrain, paving way for Bahrain independence.

events.title: Bahrain Independence
events.description: British protectorate ended, Bahrain declared independence with Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa as Emir. Bahrain joined UN and Arab League. Bahrain became small but important Gulf state, positioning as financial and commercial center.

events.title: Constitution and Parliament
events.description: Bahrain promulgated constitution, established elected National Assembly. But 1975 Emir dissolved parliament and suspended constitution citing security reasons. This opened authoritarian rule period, parliament not restored until 2002.

events.title: Parliament Dissolution
events.description: Emir Isa dissolved parliament citing national security and regional tensions (Lebanese Civil War), suspended constitution. Opposition suppressed, many activists exiled. This marked end of Bahrain's democratic experiment.

events.title: Iranian Revolution Impact
events.description: Iranian Islamic Revolution shocked Persian Gulf. Bahraini Shias influenced by Khomeini ideology, demanded reforms. Government worried Iran inciting Shia uprising, strengthened security measures.

events.title: Coup Attempt and Iranian Influence
events.description: Iran-backed Shia organization plotted failed coup in Bahrain. This intensified Bahrain's concerns about Iranian influence and domestic Shias. Bahrain joined GCC, allying with Sunni neighbors against Iranian threat.

events.title: King Fahd Causeway
events.description: King Fahd Causeway connecting Bahrain and Saudi Arabia opened. This strengthened Bahrain-Saudi economic and political ties, also making Saudi military intervention in Bahrain easier during crises.

events.title: Shia Uprising
events.description: Bahraini Shias (70% of population) launched massive protests and uprising, demanding parliament restoration, political prisoner release and end to discrimination. Government crackdown, arrested thousands, accused Iran and Hezbollah involvement. Crisis lasted until late 1990s, deeply dividing society.

events.title: Uprising Peak
events.description: Bahrain uprising reached peak, protests, violence and repression escalated. Government arrested thousands including religious leaders. Shia villages raided by security forces. Dozens killed, society highly tense.

events.title: Hamad Succeeds
events.description: Emir Isa died, son Hamad bin Isa succeeded. Hamad promised reforms, released political prisoners, allowed exiles to return. His reforms brought hope, called 'Hamad Spring.'

events.title: National Action Charter and Kingdom
events.description: Hamad proposed National Action Charter, promising parliament restoration and expanded political participation. Passed by 98% referendum. 2002 Bahrain changed from emirate to kingdom, Hamad became king. Restored elected parliament, but only lower house elected, upper house appointed by king, powers limited.

events.title: Parliament Elections Restored
events.description: Bahrain held first parliamentary elections in 27 years. Shia opposition Al-Wefaq won majority seats. But parliament powers limited, unable to pass major reforms. Many Shias felt disappointed.

events.title: US Fifth Fleet Base
events.description: Bahrain continued as US Fifth Fleet headquarters, main US military presence in Persian Gulf. This gave Bahrain important position in US strategy, but also sparked controversy.

events.title: Economic Challenges
events.description: Bahrain oil reserves depleted, economy dependent on financial services and Saudi aid. Youth unemployment high, especially among Shias. Housing shortage and rising living costs sparked discontent.

events.title: Pearl Roundabout Uprising
events.description: Inspired by Arab Spring, mainly Shia protesters occupied Manama's Pearl Roundabout, demanding constitutional reform, truly elected government and end to discrimination. Protests initially peaceful, attracting tens of thousands. After initial crackdown government withdrew, giving protesters space.

events.title: GCC Military Intervention
events.description: Saudi-led GCC Peninsula Shield forces entered Bahrain supporting government. Government declared martial law, violently cleared Pearl Roundabout, destroyed iconic monument. Crackdown killed dozens, arrested thousands. Shia mosques destroyed, activists sentenced heavily. Government claimed Iran orchestrated uprising (Iran denied).

events.title: Continued Repression and Tensions
events.description: After uprising, Bahrain intensified repression: revoking dissidents' citizenship, long imprisonments, prosecuting doctors and activists, banning major opposition organizations (like Al-Wefaq). Security forces regularly clashed with Shia villages. Human rights organizations widely criticized Bahrain. But government claimed reforms, established oversight bodies, though critics say insufficient.

events.title: Continued Protests and Crackdowns
events.description: Shia villages continued protests, security forces crackdown. Government banned mass gatherings, arrested activists. International human rights organizations criticized Bahrain human rights violations, but Western countries' criticism limited due to strategic interests.

events.title: Protests After Nimr al-Nimr Execution
events.description: After Saudi execution of Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr, Bahraini Shias protested. Bahrain government cracked down, stripped major Shia cleric Isa Qassim of citizenship, sparking more protests and international criticism.

events.title: Qatar Crisis Stance
events.description: Bahrain joined Saudi, UAE and Egypt in severing ties with Qatar, accusing it of supporting terrorism. Bahrain had worst relations with Qatar, accused Qatar of supporting Shia opposition. Relations restored 2021, but mutual trust limited.

events.title: F1 Grand Prix Controversy
events.description: Bahrain continued hosting F1 Grand Prix as international image promotion. But human rights groups used event to spotlight Bahrain's human rights situation. Government tried separating sports from politics, but criticism continued.

events.title: Normalization with Israel
events.description: Bahrain normalized relations with Israel under Abraham Accords framework, following UAE. Bahrain said move promotes peace, but Bahrainis (especially Shias) widely opposed, viewing as Palestinian betrayal.

events.title: Crown Prince Salman in Power
events.description: Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad became Bahrain's de facto ruler as King Hamad aged. Salman pushed economic diversification, attracting investment and fintech companies. But political reform limited, Shia marginalization continued.

events.title: Divided Kingdom
events.description: Bahrain remains deeply divided society: Sunni royal family ruling Shia majority (about 70% population but officially unacknowledged), Shias feel discriminated, excluded from military, security and senior positions. Limited political participation, weak parliament powers. Economically, Bahrain's oil reserves depleted, relying on Saudi aid and as financial center. Bahrain faces debt, youth unemployment and housing shortage. Bahrain struggles to maintain relevance in shadow of Saudi and UAE. But Bahrain maintains position as Gulf financial and commercial hub, hosting international events like F1 Grand Prix. Bahrain's future depends on addressing sectarian divide, achieving economic sustainability, and development of regional tensions especially Iran relations. Small complex kingdom, Bahrain's stability crucial to Gulf region.
